items.name: Resonance Striker
items.description: A short haft ending in a tuning-fork head that rings on impact — favored in the Heights. The ring does the real damage, rattling bone and mechanism alike.

items.name: Prism Lens
items.description: A palm-sized cut crystal on a thong. Held to the eye it splits light into readings; held to the sun it can throw a focused beam. Plateau-made.
items.substrateNote: Cut Radiant crystal — a focus that gathers as well as splits.

items.name: Warden's Knife
items.description: A plain, beautifully-kept blade of green-black stone, the kind the Glade wardens carry. Cuts cord and defends a life; never used for cruelty without the grove somehow knowing.

items.name: Pass-Cloak
items.description: A heavy oiled cloak from the Roost, cut for the mountain trails — sheds rain, breaks wind, and hides a lot of a person on an exposed switchback.
items._soakWhy: A heavy oiled cloak answers WEATHER, not weapons. 4 cold because that is what it is for; 1 physical because a thick wet cloak turns a graze and nothing more. ⛔ CCODE 2026-09-04: 'the player seat now carries `soak` and NOTHING WRITES IT — Pell's brigandine does nothing anywhere.' ⚠️ Four items were `kind: armor` and only `oiled_leathers` carried a value. ✅ SHAPE COPIED FROM IT — typed `soakLayers`, because a layer that names a type answers ONLY that type and is transparent to everything else (CCODE-290). ⛔ NEVER SEVERAL LAYERS FOR ONE GARMENT: three layers of 5 would be 15 soak. ⚠️ VALUES DELIBERATELY SMALL — soak is a FLAT subtraction against a median craft of 7 damage, so 2 physical is a real third of an ordinary blow, and `minHit` guarantees nothing is ever immune.

items.name: Channel Pole
items.description: A marsh-pilot's pole from the Greywater — finds the bottom, moves a skiff, tests suspect ground, and cracks a skull in a pinch. Tam swears by his.

items.name: Greenlore Satchel
items.description: A herbalist's roll of pockets and vials — poultices, teas, antidotes, and the tools to make more from what the country gives.

items.name: Quiet Boots
items.description: Soft-soled, marsh-tanned boots that make no sound on natural ground and grip wet stone. The difference between being heard and not.
items._soakWhy: ⬜ NO SOAK, DELIBERATELY. Boots that make no sound are not armour — their whole value is `stealth`/`grip` in `bonusTags`. ⚠️ Authoring soak here would make every armour SLOT a damage slot, which is how a kit becomes a spreadsheet. ⛔ CCODE 2026-09-04: 'the player seat now carries `soak` and NOTHING WRITES IT — Pell's brigandine does nothing anywhere.' ⚠️ Four items were `kind: armor` and only `oiled_leathers` carried a value. ✅ SHAPE COPIED FROM IT — typed `soakLayers`, because a layer that names a type answers ONLY that type and is transparent to everything else (CCODE-290). ⛔ NEVER SEVERAL LAYERS FOR ONE GARMENT: three layers of 5 would be 15 soak. ⚠️ VALUES DELIBERATELY SMALL — soak is a FLAT subtraction against a median craft of 7 damage, so 2 physical is a real third of an ordinary blow, and `minHit` guarantees nothing is ever immune.

items.name: Storm-Glass
items.description: A sealed glass of shifting crystal that reads the coming weather a day out. Greta keeps one at the waystation; travelers covet them.

items.name: Healer's Draught
items.description: A bitter greenlore brew that closes wounds and steadies a failing body. One dose. Tastes like wet bark and works anyway.

items.name: Clarity Tea
items.description: A pale astringent tea that burns off exhaustion and sharpens a tired mind for a while. One dose; the crash comes later.

items.name: Smoke-Bead
items.description: A clay bead that bursts into a cloud of grey concealment when thrown. One use. Runners and cutpurses buy them by the string at the Roost.

items.name: Toll-Chits
items.description: A handful of the Kestrel's stamped brass chits — the Roost's own currency of favors owed. Spend them for passage, silence, or a door opened.

items.name: Choir-Shard
items.description: A sliver of stone from the Sunken Choir's drowned tiers that will not stop faintly ringing. It sharpens sonic work — and, held too long, starts to return voices. Not for the unwary.

evolution.note: The Choir-Shard changes the longer it's carried and used in sonic work — it needs no companion, only use and time. GM foreshadows the shift; the third stage carries a cost the bearer chose by not putting it down.

stages.name: Faint Ring
stages.description: A shard that will not stop softly ringing. Sharpens sonic work a little.
stages.narrationHints: A note under everything, just at the edge of hearing.

stages.name: Answering Ring
stages.description: The shard has begun to answer your casts before you finish them — stronger sonic work, and the first whispers.
stages.grant: Sonic casts sharpen further; the GM may offer the shard 'answering' a beat early.
stages.narrationHints: It rings back now, in a voice not quite yours.

stages.name: The Voice in the Stone
stages.description: The shard has learned to return voices, like the Choir it came from. Powerful — and it wants to be listened to. Putting it down is now its own decision.
stages.grant: Strong sonic amplification; once per scene the shard offers a true reading in a returned voice — at a cost the GM names.
stages.narrationHints: It speaks in the voices of the drowned. It has been waiting for someone to keep it this long.

items.substrateNote: Stone from the drowned tiers of a pre-Transition work. It came out of a pool and it kept some.

items.name: Smith's Hammer
items.description: A cross-peen she made her second year and has never replaced. It shapes iron all day and answers a threshold at night, and she has never treated those as different uses.
items._authored_20260904: ⚑ The working tool as the weapon — `plain_weight` in her hand. ⬜ NO damage value: weapons carry `bonusTags` and the CRAFT carries the dice. ⚠️ Aevi nearly authored damage here and it would have been a second, competing source of numbers.
items._supersededNote: ⚠️ KEPT — the hammer is not in the staged record and is her working tool. ⛔ BUT `smiths_brigandine` WAS REMOVED: Aevi authored it 2026-09-04 while `po/staged_content/pell_fell_pell_gear.json` already held a canon-sourced, bestiary-MEASURED brigandine record. She did not look. ✅ `pells_brigandine` is the real one.

items.name: The Warden's Charge
items.description: A short, plain-hilted blade of Pell's own making, rune-bound at the Fell Pell with four threads — Huginn's Ashwarden ending-sense laid along the edge, Pell's own ironsense seated through the tang, and two more closed into the ricasso. It is not a showpiece. It is a smith's sword, bound by the smith who made it.
items.provenance: Forged and rune-bound by Pell Ran Marsh at the Fell Pell gathering, the night the fellowship formally opened.
items.canonQuote: Pell's short sword rune-bound with four threads including Huginn's ending-sense and her own ironsense.
items.damageTypeWhy: The first bound thread that carries a kind is Huginn's Ashwarden ending-sense → decay. Same resolution, same reason, as Silas's Memory spear from the same working. If the intended lead thread is the ironsense instead, this becomes untyped-by-tradition and the sword strikes as plain steel — which is a real difference against anything immune to physical, so it is worth deciding rather than defaulting.

threads.what: Pell's own ironsense, seated through the tang — the anchor
Huginn's ending-sense, laid along the edge

items.threadsNote: Canon says FOUR threads and names TWO. The other two are deliberately left unauthored rather than invented — Aevi or Erik should name them, and until they do the sword resolves off the two that are canon.

items.name: Pell's Warded Brigandine
items.description: A working brigandine, its plates set close and its rune-work run unbroken from collar to hem. One radiant mark sits at the chest, scraped from the last of the vial. In the outer ring a Shielding Word is seated — begun, not finished, and the gap in it is visible to anyone who can read the work.
items.provenance: Finished by Pell Ran Marsh at the Fell Pell gathering, the radiant mark taken from the vial's last scraping.
items.canonQuote: Pell's brigandine finished with full protective rune-work collar to hem, one radiant mark at the chest from the vial's last scraping, and a partial Shielding Word seated in its outer ring with the promise of completion.

wardLayers.what: the full protective rune-work, collar to hem — it answers everything
the single radiant mark at the chest

incomplete.what: the Shielding Word seated in the outer ring, partial
incomplete.mechanicalProposal: It is NOT a layer yet. A partial working that already soaked would make finishing it a formality, and the chronicle plainly frames completion as a thing still owed. Proposed: finishing it adds a rank-3 layer — the first rank-3 ward in the world — which is why it is worth a scene rather than a line.
incomplete.whoDecides: Erik — whether the finished Word is a third layer, a rank promotion of the existing rune-work, or something that is not soak at all.
